text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The leadership of Bulgaria's ruling Socialist party approved a draft Socialist cabinet despite opposition protests and nationwide strikes.

Under the draft the outgoing finance, trade and energy ministers retain their posts. The U.S.-born Georgi Pirinski, who resigned as foreign minister in November, returns to the foreign ministry and becomes a deputy prime minister.
-- The Socialist premier-designate Nikolai Dobrev would present today the list to President Petar Stoyanov and it is expected to be voted in parliament on Wednesday.
-- Three members of the Socialist parliamentary group opposed forming a second Socialist cabinet and said they were not going to support it in parliament.

-- Strikes and roadblocks paralysed Bulgaria on Monday in protest against forming of a second Socialist cabinet. Soppages were expected today at Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftohim and Kremikovtsi steel works.
-- Leaders of Bulgaria's opposition appealed to members of all parliamentary groups to vote against the second Socialist cabinet.
-- Prince Kiril, son of Bulgaria's exiled King Simeon, has agreed to act as a consultant to Bulgaria president's economic council, President Stoyanov told leading local economists.
-- A bomb exploded in the car of the former military prosecutor General Lilko Yotsov, badly injuring him and his wife, police said.
-- Russia's oil company Rosneft said it had cut crude oil supplies to Bulgaria's largest oil refinery Neftohim over unpaid debts and political unstability in Bulgaria.

-- Bulgaria's power supplies have not been hit yet by the general strike organised by the opposition supporters and there is no danger of power rationing, a National Electricity Company spokesman said.
